title: Create tone-interaction map and proportional elevation curves for compact components
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Rationalize interactive color and elevation behavior for compact components across density modes. Deliver a tone-interaction mapping that defines how base palette colors move through hover/pressed/focus/disabled states using perceptually-linear ramps, and produce a proportional elevation curve (shadow and blur values) that scales based on component footprint and container density.
background: Current token set has discrete color deltas and fixed elevation steps borrowed from the full-density system. Compact components (small buttons, dense rows, micro-cards) feel visually inconsistent: hover highlights can look too saturated, pressed states collapse contrast, and shadows either disappear or over-bleed on small surfaces. Engineers have requested a shareable, parametric token surface that they can consume in runtime (JS/JSON) to derive states programmatically.
scope: Design system token specification and component guidance for: (1) color interaction ramps for primary/neutral/accent/critical palettes, (2) a proportional elevation curve that outputs shadow layers for small/medium/large compact surfaces, (3) radius scaling rules for asymmetric corner needs (e.g., pill vs. micro-card), and (4) samples + migration notes for buttons, table rows, and compact chart cards.
deliverables: Tone-interaction mapping document (Figma + Confluence) with color deltas and WCAG contrast checks
Proportional elevation curve: formula and lookup table for 0-4 density steps
Radius-scaling guidance with token examples for 3 shape families
Token JSON prototype (tokens/tone-interaction-compact.json) for engineering consumption
Migration notes and a short dev checklist for backwards compatibility
decisions: Adopt perceptual (CAM02-UCS) color interpolation for ramps rather than linear sRGB to avoid mid-step contrast collapse
Provide parametric elevation generator and small static lookup for backward compatibility; runtime will prefer generator when available
Use asymmetric radius tokens with named families (radius-pill, radius-card-micro, radius-button-compact) to minimize per-component overrides
tradeoffs: Perceptual ramps require build tooling to convert CAM02-UCS deltas to sRGB for runtime — increases build complexity but yields more predictable visual steps
Proportional elevation sacrifices pixel-identical parity with current heavy shadows to improve readability on small surfaces; some legacy screens will look flatter
Introducing parametric tokens requires an initial engineering adapter; avoids repeating token variants but adds integration work
tasks: Finalize delta values for hover/pressed/focus/disabled for each palette (Aisha)
Author elevation curve and run cross-platform raster tests (Liam)
Create tokens JSON and publish to tokens repo (Design + Platform)
Implement example button/table-card stories in Storybook (Frontend)
Run automated contrast checks against common content patterns and collect QA screenshots (QA)
acceptance_criteria: Tone-interaction ramps demonstrate monotonic contrast change across states and pass WCAG AA for primary button text in typical usage
Elevation curve produces shadow stacks that are legible at 16px and 24px component heights without visual bleeding
Design tokens JSON consumed by a sample frontend app matches the visual spec within a 2px tolerance for shadow spread/offset
Migration guide contains a fallback plan and a list of top 10 components to update with code examples
